newsitem.title: UK: Police probe N.Ireland explosion - agency.
newsitem.headline: Police probe N.Ireland explosion - agency.

text.p: Police were investigating an explosion early on Monday at the offices of the IRA's political wing Sinn Fein in the Northern Ireland city of Londonderry, Britain's Press Association news agency said.
The agency quoted a police spokesman as saying there were no casualties but the offices had been damaged.
"We are investigating a blast and fire at the Sinn Fein offices. At this stage we don't know what caused the explosion," the spokesman was quoted as saying.
Sinn Fein on Sunday challenged the winner of Britain's general election on May 1 to lift a ban on its entry to Northern Ireland peace talks and negotiate a lasting settlement.

Sinn Fein president Gerry Adams told a party conference that Sinn Fein votes in the election would put pressure on the British government and pro-British Unionist parties to end the ban and talk. Sinn Fein is contesting 17 of the 18 Northern Ireland constituencies and is confident of winning two to three seats.

Britain, Ireland and the United States have banned all contact with Sinn Fein since the Irish Republican Army (IRA) ended a 17-month ceasefire in its war against British rule in Northern Ireland in February 1996.
